messages.subject: [g.part2] and [g.part3]: wrongly detected inactivity bouts
parts:
Hi Vincent and hi everyone,

I am using GGIR (ver. 1.9.1) on Axivity Ax3 data to measure sleep, but I am experiencing a problem in the g.part.3 inactivity bouts detection and, possibly, already in g.part.2.
The problem consists in inactivity bouts not corresponding to participant activity, as shown in the example below:

Here, the g.part3 meta output (sib.cla.sum, attached to this message) shows the first two inactivity bouts respectively from 01:05:05 to 01:14:55 and from 02:30:35 to 02:47:30. However, as you can see, there is  (1) no reason to end the first bout at 01:15 because the arm angle does not change, (2) no reason to start the second bout only at 02:30, since there are no evident movements meanwhile, and (3) it is not clear why the second bout ends only at 2:47 despite a clear movement at 02:40:46. This is the raw Ax3 recording:


I believe that the problem orignins already in g.part2, where intervals of stable arm angle (*) are classified as vigorous activity and it is not clear why only few inactivity intervals are considered as sleep/rest. Here you can see the g.part2 file summary report:


This is just an example, but the same applies to other nights and participants, using both the shell function and the separate g.part2 and g.part3 functions. Where do you think the error comes from? Which part2 or part3 arguments could I change to have an accurate detection?

Below I report both the shell  and the g.part2 and 3 arguments I have used, and I attach to this message the "meta" results of g.part1, 2 and 3 for this participant.
I thank you in advance,
Luca

INPUT.dir <- "C:/path.to.data"
OUTPUT.dir <- "C:/path.to.output"

# shell function
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

             #-------------------------------
             timethreshold= c(5,10),
             anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,

             # Part 4 parameters:

             outliers.only = FALSE,
             criterror = 4,

             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,

             threshold.lig = c(30,40,50),
             threshold.mod = c(100,120),
             threshold.vig = c(400,500),

             boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
             boutdur.in = c(10,20,30),
             boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),
             timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------

             #-------------------------------

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# part2 and 3 separately
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

g.part2(datadir=INPUT.dir,
        metadatadir=paste(OUTPUT.dir,"/output_",basename(INPUT.dir),sep=""),
        f0=1,f1=1,
        desiredtz="Europe/London",
        overwrite=TRUE,
        
        # settings left as default values
        strategy = 1,
        hrs.del.start = 0.5,hrs.del.end = 0.5, maxdur = 7, 
        includedaycrit = 16, L5M5window = c(0,24), M5L5res = 10, 
        winhr = 5, qwindow=c(0,24), qlevels = c(0.1),
        ilevels = c(0,10), mvpathreshold = c(100),
        boutcriter = 0.8,ndayswindow=3,idloc=1,
        do.imp=TRUE,storefolderstructure=FALSE,
        epochvalues2csv=FALSE, mvpadur=c(1,5,10),selectdaysfile=c(),
        window.summary.size=100,dayborder=0,
        bout.metric=2,closedbout=FALSE,
        IVIS_windowsize_minutes = 60, IVIS_epochsize_seconds = 3600,
        iglevels = c())

g.part3(metadatadir=paste(OUTPUT.dir,"/output_",basename(INPUT.dir),sep=""),
        desiredtz="Europe/London",
        f0=1,f1=1,
        overwrite=TRUE,
        
        # settings left as default values
        anglethreshold = 5,
        timethreshold = 5,
        acc.metric="ENMO", 
        ignorenonwear=TRUE,
        constrain2range=TRUE,
        do.part3.pdf=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] [g.part2] and [g.part3]: wrongly detected inactivity bouts
parts:
Hi Luca,

I just had a look.

GGIR detects 26.6% of your recording as signal clipping, indicating
that the acceleration signal was near the edge of the dynamic range
for a substantial amount of time. I rarely see this, and it can
indicate that there is something wrong with the accelerometer.

Next, GGIR imputes those clipping periods, and this is why the
sustained inactivity bout (sleep) classifications does not match the
pattern in the raw signal. GGIR is using the impute values and not the
raw values. If I remember correctly this is not something you can
easily turn off as a user.

To get to the cause of the problem:
1. Are you using the Axivity with a dynamic range setting different than 8g?
2. Do you spot anything in the acceleration signal within OMGui that
indicates extreme values?
3. Have you tried processing the cwa files as well as the
wav-converted files? It would be interesting to see whether the
problem is consistent between file formats.

Also I notice that you processed the data with anglethreshold = 1,
rahter than 5, but I do not think that is the problem.

Best wishes,
Vincent
